summary: Stripe sandbox payment integration tested end-to-end. Backend: added TestPayments class (7 tests) to /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covering health root, invalid booking_id (404), valid checkout creating a cs_test_... session + payment_transactions row (initiated/pending), status endpoint for pending/unknown, webhook signature validation (400 on invalid), and simulated-paid settlement that flips booking.status to 'approved' and surfaces in /properties/{id}/bookings. All 27/27 pytest tests pass. Frontend: /pagamento/sucesso?session_id=<bogus> correctly shows 'Não encontramos esse pagamento' (unknown session 404 -> error phase). /pagamento/sucesso with no session_id also shows error. /pagamento/cancelado renders cancel screen with WhatsApp button. On /casa/ps-01, data-testid=property-pay-now-btn is visible; clicking without dates shows 'Selecione as datas de check-in e check-out' toast. After selecting dates in shadcn calendar, clicking pay-now issues POST /api/bookings then POST /api/payments/checkout and redirects window.location.href to https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_... — Stripe hosted checkout loads showing 'Reserva — Casa Mirante Taperapuã · R$ 2.800,00' in BRL with pt-BR locale (verified via screenshot).

issues: Only tested the paid/error/missing-session paths with real Stripe sandbox; the 'pending' phase (reached after 15 polls on a never-paid session) is reachable but was not exercised in UI to avoid 30s wait. Flow verified via code review — polls every 2s then sets phase='pending' with Clock + WhatsApp button.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 637 lines — still readable, but Stripe payment endpoints (~140 lines) could be split into /app/backend/routers/payments.py for separation of concerns. Not blocking.

GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} calls stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve on every poll if payment_status != 'paid'. With 15 polls per client × many concurrent users this can rate-limit against Stripe. Consider skipping retrieve when txn is in a terminal state (failed/expired) and/or caching the last retrieval timestamp for a few seconds.

_settle_paid_session is called from both GET /payments/status and POST /stripe/webhook. The DB update_many filter uses payment_status: {'$ne': 'paid'} which gives atomic idempotency on the txn row, but the subsequent booking update is NOT guarded by the same filter — if two requests race, both will issue the identical bookings.update_one. Not a correctness bug (idempotent $set) but worth guarding with status: {'$ne': 'approved'} for the audit log.

/api/payments/checkout accepts origin_url verbatim from the client — any arbitrary URL is used as success_url/cancel_url prefix. For a sandbox this is fine, but in production this should be validated against an allow-list of origins to prevent open-redirect / phishing patterns in abandoned Stripe sessions.

payment_transactions collection has no index on session_id — the status endpoint does a find_one by session_id on every poll. Add db.payment_transactions.create_index('session_id', unique=True) in startup().
CheckoutRequest does not validate origin_url as a URL (plain str). Use pydantic HttpUrl or AnyHttpUrl to reject malformed origins and give a 422 instead of letting Stripe fail.

Frontend PaymentSuccess.jsx: when the first poll already returns payment_status='paid' it sets attempts=0 which is fine, but if api.get rejects (network blip) it immediately moves to phase='error' with no retry. Consider retrying transient errors a couple of times before showing 'Não encontramos esse pagamento'.
